Entry.JapaneseText: おばあちゃん娘
Entry.EnglishText: Grandma's Little Girl

Entry.JapaneseText: 教育ママ
Entry.EnglishText: Tiger Mom

Entry.JapaneseText: 昔話こばばぁ
Entry.EnglishText: Tale-Teller Granny

Entry.JapaneseText: 口の悪い少女
Entry.EnglishText: Foul-Mouthed Boy

Entry.JapaneseText: 昔話ばばぁ
Entry.EnglishText: Granny, Teller of Tales

Entry.JapaneseText: 逃げてきた兵士
Entry.EnglishText: Fleeing Soldier

Entry.JapaneseText: 平和を喜ぶ老婆
Entry.EnglishText: Peace-Enjoying Old Woman

Entry.JapaneseText: 保護をした老人
Entry.EnglishText: Refuge-Giving Old Man

Entry.JapaneseText: ふーん、へぇ…… ほぉ……
Entry.EnglishText: Hmm... Huh... Oooh...

Entry.JapaneseText: ちょっと！ おばあちゃんの話 聞いてるんだから 邪魔しないで！
Entry.EnglishText: Hey! I'm trying to listen to Grandma's story! Butt out already!

Entry.JapaneseText: おばあちゃんの話は とても面白いんだ
Entry.EnglishText: My grandma's stories are all so interesting.

Entry.JapaneseText: 勉強するよりも ずっと面白いよ
Entry.EnglishText: They're way, way more interesting than studying.

Entry.JapaneseText: 村の植物が枯れたり動物が あんまり見えなくなったのは マナが少なくなったからなんだよ
Entry.EnglishText: The plants were all withering and the animals had all but disappeared because of the lack of mana.

Entry.JapaneseText: ……おばあちゃんが 言ってたんだけどね
Entry.EnglishText: ...Or that's what my grandma told me!

Entry.JapaneseText: 本当にうちの おばあちゃんって 物知りなんだよ
Entry.EnglishText: My grandma knows a whole lot of things, actually.

Entry.JapaneseText: 「知恵星の一族」だって言ってたけど 本当かな？ それ何なんだろ？
精霊の話、魔界の話、 ふしぎな種族の話、 空を飛ぶほうき星の話……
Entry.EnglishText: Stories about spirits, and ones about Daemonium, and mysterious tribes, and comets...

Entry.JapaneseText: おばあちゃんは、 無限にお話の湧き上がる 泉のようなんだ
Entry.EnglishText: My grandma's like a fountain, but bubbling over with endless stories, instead of water.

Entry.JapaneseText: よーし、私も おばあちゃんのような お話おばばになるぞー！
Entry.EnglishText: Alright, I'm gonna be a storytelling granny one day, too!

Entry.JapaneseText: うちのお義母さんったら しょうもない話ばかり……
Entry.EnglishText: My mother-in-law just never stops telling all these silly stories...

Entry.JapaneseText: このままでは うちの娘がダメになるわ
Entry.EnglishText: At this rate, my daughter will grow up to be a useless bum!

Entry.JapaneseText: まったく、うちの娘には まっとうになってほしいわ
Entry.EnglishText: My word. I just want my daughter to be a respectable member of society someday.

Entry.JapaneseText: ちゃんと勉強に身を入れて しっかりした社会の人に……
Entry.EnglishText: If she could just devote herself to her studies, and go to work for a good company...

Entry.JapaneseText: 精霊とか小鬼とか 古代大戦とかユニコーンとか……
Entry.EnglishText: Spirits and imps and ancient wars and unicorns...

Entry.JapaneseText: そんなこと知っても 何の役にも立たないのよ！
Entry.EnglishText: There's no sense in filling your head with all that fluff! It's useless!

Entry.JapaneseText: ミッドガルズ経済の衰亡とか ヴェネツィア式商業戦略とか アルヴァニスタの魔法流通とか
Entry.EnglishText: Midgard's economic collapse, Venezian School trade policy, Alvanista's flow of magic...

Entry.JapaneseText: そういう現実的な話を してほしいのに……！
Entry.EnglishText: Why won't she tell her about the real, important things, with real consequences...!

Entry.JapaneseText: マズイわ…… うちの娘が確実に 道を踏み外しているわ……
Entry.EnglishText: This is bad... I'm certain now... My daughter's strayed from the path...

Entry.JapaneseText: どうしましょう…… このままではお義母さんみたいに なってしまう……
Entry.EnglishText: What can I do...? She's going to turn out like my mother-in-law...

Entry.JapaneseText: うちの子は本当に困った娘！ 過去の失敗や幻想からなんて 何も学べないのよ！
Entry.EnglishText: My child's always such a difficult girl! You can't learn anything from the failures and fantasies of the past!

Entry.JapaneseText: 見るなら今！ 今、社会で何が起こっているか、 そうじゃなくて？
Entry.EnglishText: You have to focus on the present! "What are the companies of today doing?"! Isn't that what's important?

Entry.JapaneseText: むかーしむかし、 この近くの洞窟に 火の精霊がおったのよ
Entry.EnglishText: A long, long time ago, a great spirit of fire lived in a cavern not far from here.

Entry.JapaneseText: でも、人が あまりうるさくするもんで 引越ししたんだとさ
Entry.EnglishText: But, people were noisy and troublesome, so the spirit moved far away.

Entry.JapaneseText: 精霊はいなくなって、 洞窟もすっかり埋まったんだ
Entry.EnglishText: After the spirit left, the cavern itself was soon buried, too.

Entry.JapaneseText: どこへ 行っちまったのかの……
Entry.EnglishText: I wonder where that spirit went...

Entry.JapaneseText: むかーしむかし、 精霊王の住む森の奥には 更に奥があったんだと
Entry.EnglishText: A long, long time ago, the forest where the King of Spirits lives went much deeper than it does today.

Entry.JapaneseText: 相応の精神力を持つ人間しか その秘境には入り込めなかった という話よ
Entry.EnglishText: It's said that only humans with sufficient power of will could gain entry to those hidden lands.

Entry.JapaneseText: そこには不思議な生物や 魔物がたんと 住んどったんだと
Entry.EnglishText: And many wondrous animals and monsters dwelled there.

Entry.JapaneseText: それは精霊王の精神世界では ないかとも言われとるぞ
Entry.EnglishText: Some have said those lands were a manifestation of the King of Spirits' own will.

Entry.JapaneseText: むかーしむかし、地下世界には ドワーフという手先が器用な 地の者がいたんだと
Entry.EnglishText: A long, long time ago, people known as dwarves lived beneath us. They were people of the earth, and deft of hand.

Entry.JapaneseText: 精霊の洞窟におる クレイアイドルもその一族から 派生した者たちらしいぞ？
Entry.EnglishText: And it seems the Clay Idols who dwell in the Cave of Spirits are counted among their relatives...

Entry.JapaneseText: 精霊たちと契約できる……
Entry.EnglishText: You can make a pact with the spirits...

Entry.JapaneseText: ……おや、おぬしらとは どこかで会ったかの？ １００年、くらい、前……
Entry.EnglishText: ...Oh, my. Haven't I met all of you before, somewhere? About one hundred years past...

Entry.JapaneseText: うちのばばぁは 役に立たない話ばっか しやがってよ！
Entry.EnglishText: My granny's always talkin' about all this worthless nonsense!

Entry.JapaneseText: こんな平和な時代に 精霊もへったくれも ないっていうの
Entry.EnglishText: Spirit's'd just be useless junk in a peaceful world like ours, anyway.

Entry.JapaneseText: ダオスだ？ そんなもんは１００年も前に やられたアホだろ？
Entry.EnglishText: Huh, Dhaos? Didn't that moron get his ass kicked, like, 100 years ago?

Entry.JapaneseText: よみがえったとかいう噂もあった けどあの後、何もなかったし、 デマだったんだろ？
Entry.EnglishText: Some people were sayin' he'd been resurrected, but not a damn thing's happened since. Just a buncha BS!

Entry.JapaneseText: 精霊がどうしたって？ そんな話聞いても 腹なんか膨れねーっての
Entry.EnglishText: What happened to the spirits? C'mon, who cares? Learnin' about all that crap won't put food in your belly!

Entry.JapaneseText: 精霊が食えんのか？ 精霊で銭金がもうかんのか？
Entry.EnglishText: What are ya gonna do, try and eat the spirits? Put 'em to work in the fields?

Entry.JapaneseText: 本当にうちのばばぁの話は 長いんだ
Entry.EnglishText: My granny talks way too much.

Entry.JapaneseText: 全部聞いてたら 日が登って沈んで また朝が来るんだ
Entry.EnglishText: I tried to listen to all she's got to say, and the sun went down and came back up again before she finished her yappin'.

Entry.JapaneseText: おかげで眠くて しかたねー！！
Entry.EnglishText: And now I'm too damn tired to do anything!

Entry.JapaneseText: ドワーフとか、エルフとか もういい加減、 うざい話が多すぎだぜ！
Entry.EnglishText: Dwarves this, elves that, just shut the hell up already!

Entry.JapaneseText: でも可哀想だから聞いてやるぜ
Entry.EnglishText: But I feel bad for her, so I listen anyway.

Entry.JapaneseText: ふん、オレっていい孫だろ？
Entry.EnglishText: Hmph. I'm a real good grandkid, aren't I?

Entry.JapaneseText: ばばぁの話聞いたら １０００ガルドもらえるからな、 一応、聞いてやるぜ
Entry.EnglishText: I'll get 1000 Gald if I listen to her stories, so I guess I'll try and listen.

Entry.JapaneseText: ……そんなとこで聞いてても おまえらはもらえねーぞ！？
Entry.EnglishText: ...Even if you stand there and listen in, too, you guys won't get a damned thing!

Entry.JapaneseText: むかーしむかし、 この近くの洞窟に 火の精霊がおったそうな
Entry.EnglishText: A long, long time ago, a great spirit of fire dwelt in a cavern near here.

Entry.JapaneseText: 多くの人に敬われ まつられておったそうな
Entry.EnglishText: That spirit was revered and respected by many, many people.

Entry.JapaneseText: 今もおるのかの？
Entry.EnglishText: I wonder if that spirit's still there now?

Entry.JapaneseText: 今も洞窟はあるが、 精霊様に会った者はいないそうな
Entry.EnglishText: The cavern's there even now, but I've never heard of anyone alive today having seen the spirit.

Entry.JapaneseText: 気配はあるそうじゃがの……
Entry.EnglishText: But you can still feel a presence in there, can't you...

Entry.JapaneseText: むかーしむかし、 精霊王の住む森の奥には 更に奥があったそうな
Entry.EnglishText: A long, long time ago, the forest where the King of Spirits lives went far deeper than it goes today.

Entry.JapaneseText: 相応の精神力を持つ人間しか その秘境には入り込めなかった という話じゃ
Entry.EnglishText: It's said that only humans with appropriate power of will would gain entry to those hidden lands.

Entry.JapaneseText: 今でも精霊王の森の奥の奥を 目指す者は後を絶たんそうじゃが そこへ行った者の話を聞かん
Entry.EnglishText: Even now, countless people try to find those forest depths, but you'll never hear of one who's been there.

Entry.JapaneseText: じゃが、それは本当にあるのじゃ
Entry.EnglishText: But it's true, they do exist...

Entry.JapaneseText: むかーしむかし、地下世界には ドワーフという手先が器用な 地の者がいたそうな
Entry.EnglishText: A long, long time ago, people known as dwarves lived beneath us. They were people of the ground, and skilled of hand.

Entry.JapaneseText: 精霊の洞窟におる クレイアイドルもその一族から 派生した者たちらしいぞ？
Entry.EnglishText: And it seems the Clay Idols who dwell in the Cave of Spirits are counted among their relatives...

Entry.JapaneseText: 精霊たちと契約できる 指輪はそのドワーフが 作ったものらしいじゃ
Entry.EnglishText: You can make a pact with the spirits with the rings those dwarves created, or so it seems.

Entry.JapaneseText: 今や精霊の存在自体、 ウソだと言われとるがの
Entry.EnglishText: Though many now say the existence of the spirits themselves is nothing but lies.

Entry.JapaneseText: もういやだ……オレさ 戦争コワくて アルヴァニスタから逃げてきたんだ
Entry.EnglishText: I just can't do it anymore... I'm terrified of war, so I fled here from Alvanista.

Entry.JapaneseText: もうあそこには 戻らない……
Entry.EnglishText: I'm never going back there again...

Entry.JapaneseText: え？ 戦争終わった？
Entry.EnglishText: Eh? The war's over?

Entry.JapaneseText: ウソだ、きっと街に戻れば また魔物軍団と戦わされるんだ！
Entry.EnglishText: No way! If I go back there, they'll make me fight against that army of monsters again! I'm sure of it!

Entry.JapaneseText: どうして、戦争なんてするんだ。 勝ち目がないんだから、 さっさと降伏すればいいのに……
Entry.EnglishText: Why are they even fighting this war? There's no way they'll win... They should just surrender already...

Entry.JapaneseText: え？ ダオスに 勝った！
Entry.EnglishText: Eh? They beat Dhaos!?

Entry.JapaneseText: ウソつけ！ そんなわけないだろ！
Entry.EnglishText: Stop lying! There's no way they could pull that off!

Entry.JapaneseText: ああ…… この街は平和でいいな……
Entry.EnglishText: Ahh... This town's so peaceful... It's nice...

Entry.JapaneseText: 温かいし、 アルヴァニスタとは大違いだ……
Entry.EnglishText: And it's warm, too... It's so different from Alvanista...

Entry.JapaneseText: もう２度と、 あんな国には 帰らないぞ……
Entry.EnglishText: I swear, I'm never going back to that country again...

Entry.JapaneseText: 気温ばかりか 人も冷たいからな
Entry.EnglishText: You know, it's not just the weather. Even the people there are cold.

Entry.JapaneseText: ダオスとの戦争で 多くの人が死んだって 言うね
Entry.EnglishText: They say a lot of people died in the war against Dhaos.

Entry.JapaneseText: でも、この辺りは ほとんど被害はないのさ
Entry.EnglishText: But very little of that affected us out here.

Entry.JapaneseText: アルヴァニスタにユークリッド大陸、 たくさん死人が出たってね
Entry.EnglishText: I've heard there were a great many casualties in Alvanista and the continent of Euclid, especially.

Entry.JapaneseText: 一体、ダオスってのはどうして そんな凶悪なことを したんだい？
Entry.EnglishText: But why in the world did this "Dhaos" do such terrible things?

Entry.JapaneseText: 私たちはこんな辺境の田舎に 住んでいてよかったよ
Entry.EnglishText: It's a good thing we live in such a remote, rural village.

Entry.JapaneseText: ダオス戦役とは まったくの無縁だったからね
Entry.EnglishText: Because that meant Dhaos's War had nothing at all to do with us.

Entry.JapaneseText: ダオスとの苛烈な戦いが あったのも終わった３か月くらい 後に聞いたからね
Entry.EnglishText: In fact, roughly three months had already passed before we even heard about that vicious battle with Dhaos.

Entry.JapaneseText: 本当、そんなことが あったなんてびっくりだよ
Entry.EnglishText: We were totally shocked, actually.

Entry.JapaneseText: この辺りは、 ダオス戦役の被害は まったくないんだ
Entry.EnglishText: Dhaos's War just didn't affect us in the slightest out here.

Entry.JapaneseText: この村は戦争に参加した国々に 属してないからね
Entry.EnglishText: This village doesn't belong to any of the countries that fought in that war, you see.

Entry.JapaneseText: まったく、この村は平和な村だよ
Entry.EnglishText: This village has always been peaceful.

Entry.JapaneseText: 住みづらいけれど こういう時にこの村に 住んでてよかったと思うよ
Entry.EnglishText: It's not the easiest place to live, but at times like this, I'm glad I live here.

Entry.JapaneseText: アルヴァニスタから 逃げてきた人をうちで 保護しています
Entry.EnglishText: I'm providing refuge to a man who fled here from Alvanista.

Entry.JapaneseText: もし探しているお身内の方を 見つけたらお知らせください
Entry.EnglishText: If you happen to find any relatives who are looking for him, please let me know.

Entry.JapaneseText: ご本人が国にお帰りに なりたがってないのです。 戦争が終わったことも信じず……
Entry.EnglishText: He doesn't wish to return to his country, himself. He doesn't believe the war is over...

Entry.JapaneseText: 正直、 我々も困っています
Entry.EnglishText: To be blunt, he's been a lot of trouble for us.

Entry.JapaneseText: アルヴァニスタの元兵士という方を お世話しております
Entry.EnglishText: I'm looking after a man who was formerly a soldier of Alvanista.

Entry.JapaneseText: 正直、うちも裕福でないので、 早く出ていってほしいです
Entry.EnglishText: To be blunt, we're not rich ourselves, and we'd like him to leave sooner rather than later.

Entry.JapaneseText: 情けをかけて 砂漠で行き倒れになっているのを 助けてしまったばかりに……
Entry.EnglishText: I found him collapsed in the desert, and was kind enough to save him, but...

Entry.JapaneseText: さっさと追い出してしまえば よいのですが……
Entry.EnglishText: I ought to have chased him out as soon as he came to, really...

Entry.JapaneseText: うちでお預かりしてる 元兵士の方が 我が家に住み着こうとしています
Entry.EnglishText: The former soldier I've been looking after has started treating this as his own home.

Entry.JapaneseText: ピンチです、ばあさん。 なんとかしなければいけませんよ
Entry.EnglishText: This isn't good, honey. We're going to have to do something about him.

Entry.JapaneseText: いくら人のいい我々でも 永住されては困ります
Entry.EnglishText: However kind-hearted we may be, we just can't have him living here forever.

Entry.JapaneseText: 老い先短いとは言え 勘弁勘弁
Entry.EnglishText: I know we won't live that much longer ourselves, but...
